_comment: Valmera render box admission + slots. 8 shared vCPU / 24 GB. Each slot's --cpus is a ceiling for ONE job (a lone preview may use 2 cores, a final 4), not a reservation: the slots oversubscribe the CPU on purpose and per-call cgroup CPU weights (cpu_shares: customers about 5x the owner factory under cgroup v2) divide it under contention. Memory limits are the measured p95 with headroom; batch slots have Cloudflare's 12 GiB (an owner final has peaked at 10.2 GiB there; admission's memory budget, not the slot limit, bounds what runs at once). X1 (30 Oct 2026), the owner's target: every customer, trial and MCP call plus at most 2 podcast runs (a coordinator and up to 3 editors each), customers first. The owner factory (user 60) is capped per lane (interactive 4 of 8, batch 2 of 5, mcp 6 of 10) AND leaves a customer reserve (owner_leave_free_by_lane: it starts on an ordinary slot only while that many other ordinary slots of the lane stay free; its children too), so a customer never waits behind the factory; the reserve was sized from 30 days of real customer concurrency (peaks: interactive 4, batch 8 = one user's 8-file upload, mcp 6). Memory is the box's binding resource (L4, 30 Oct: an idle slot holds ~0.25 GiB, so slots are not free): the factory's HEAVY calls (estimate above light_gib) stay within owner_mem_budget_gib of committed estimates and start only while MemAvailable minus their FULL estimate keeps owner_mem_headroom_gib beyond mem_reserve_gib, so a factory final that grows after it starts never takes the memory a customer's next render needs; light calls (MCP tools, agent turns, frame looks) are governed by real memory alone and never held behind another class's memory reservation. Quick slots serve synchronous children only. Parity: interactive slots see 2 CPUs and batch slots 4 (cpusets), exactly what Cloudflare's standard-3/standard-4 lanes expose, because x264's thread count follows the visible CPUs: with that the box renders bit-identical files (29 Oct parity gate); admission picks the free slot whose CPU set is least busy. New slots are appended with new ports so existing slots keep theirs.

shared_cache._comment: E3 (30 Oct 2026): one host directory, mounted into every slot, holds the content-addressed motion clips, plate moments and picture-check answers (MOTION_CACHE_DIR, RENDER_MEMO=1), so a short's next render on any slot reuses what an earlier one measured. boxctl clean ages it out (max_age_days, 6 h when the disk is tight).
